entries.mechanism: TAXSIM runs at its latest 2024 law year; the 2026 pipeline uses the California brackets, standard deduction, and exemption credit carried forward from the Franchise Tax Board 2025 published schedule under the section 17041(h) CCPI indexation. For the married 300,000-dollar filer the 2026 pipeline reports 19241.60 and TAXSIM 2024 reports 19650.79, a 409.19-dollar gap. The 2024 brackets are narrower (less inflation indexation), so the same taxable income reaches higher marginal rates sooner, raising the 2024 tax above the 2026 value; the gap is the two years of bracket indexation, not a pipeline defect.

For the single 30,000-dollar filer the 2026 pipeline reports 216.11 and TAXSIM 2024 reports 185.05, a positive 31.06-dollar gap (the pipeline is higher). At this income the 2024-to-2026 bracket indexation lowers the 2026 tax only slightly, and TAXSIM's siitax nets a refundable California EITC that this statutory core (RTC 17041 tax less the 17054 nonrefundable credit) excludes, pulling the TAXSIM value below the pipeline. The residual combines the indexation vintage and the refundable-credit scope difference, both documented boundaries of this core pipeline.

For the single 60,000-dollar filer the 2026 pipeline reports 1602.86 and TAXSIM 2024 reports 1693.41, a -90.55-dollar gap. TAXSIM runs at its latest 2024 law year with narrower (less inflation-indexed) brackets, so the same taxable income is taxed slightly higher in 2024; the gap is the 2024-to- 2026 bracket indexation plus, at lower incomes, the refundable California EITC that TAXSIM nets and this statutory core excludes.
